title: Inference placement for real-time on-device video analysis
prompt: You're building an app that analyzes a live camera feed on phones and smart cameras (e.g., detecting objects/events frame-by-frame) and reacts instantly in the UI. Where should the vision model run?
constraint: Reactions must be real-time (sub-frame latency, no round-trip stalls), and raw video must NOT leave the device — both for privacy and to avoid saturating uplink bandwidth.

options.why: Keeps every frame local, so there's no uplink of raw video (satisfies the bandwidth + privacy constraint) and no network round-trip per frame (satisfies real-time latency). The constraint explicitly rules out streaming raw video, which is exactly what on-device avoids — best fit, even at the cost of a smaller/quantized model.

Defensible: the real-time path stays local and only derived metadata (not raw frames) leaves the device, so it can respect privacy and latency. But it adds system complexity and a cloud dependency the constraint doesn't require for the core loop — weaker than pure on-device unless you genuinely need cloud-scale analytics.

Directly violates the constraint: it ships raw video off-device (privacy + bandwidth failure) and adds a network round-trip per frame, which kills real-time responsiveness on flaky or mobile networks. Tempting because cloud GPUs run the most accurate models, but accuracy isn't the stated priority here.

Batch processing is inherently not real-time — results arrive seconds-to-minutes late, breaking the instant-reaction requirement. It also still uploads raw video, violating the privacy/bandwidth constraint. Reasonable for offline analytics, wrong for a live reactive feed.
